title: Slate memory ledger: predictive budgeting for weights, KV and activations
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: As model sizes and concurrent traffic grow, GPUs must balance resident weights, per-request KV cache, and transient activation allocations. We currently observe tail latency spikes and degraded throughput when KV pressure and activations collide with weight residency limits. This ticket proposes a "Slate memory ledger" — a predictive per-GPU budgeting layer that tracks reserved headroom for weights, KV caches, and activations, and exposes corrective actions (eviction, inflight batching throttles, model variant fallback).

Goals:
- Provide an explicit, observable accounting of memory commitments per GPU: weights (resident + streaming), KV occupancy (active prefixes + reserved slab), and activation pool.
- Predict short-term headroom using recent allocation trends (rolling 60s + 5s burst window) and request-level token estimates so scheduler can accept/reject or route.
- Reduce tail latency from memory-related stalls by 30% and reduce OOM incidents by 90% in heavy KV workloads.
- Surface a small set of operator controls in Console for emergency headroom increases and automated fallback policies.

High-level approach:
1) Lightweight ledger: implement a fixed-structure ledger per GPU that records three counters as time series strings: weights_reserved_bytes, kv_reserved_bytes, activation_reserved_bytes. Ledger accepts delta updates at allocation/free time and exposes a predicted_headroom_bytes calculated via an EWMA of recent deltas.
2) Request scoring: extend router to attach an estimated memory footprint to each request based on model version, sequence length, kv_prefix_length and batch size. Use that estimate when considering queue admission.
3) Admission policy: if predicted_headroom_bytes < estimated_request_footprint, either queue the request into a slow-path batch, route to a model-variant with lower memory profile, or reject with backpressure depending on customer tier. Policy is configurable per pool.
4) KV cache slab strategy: replace current global LRU with a two-tier slab allocation where small prefixes use a fast slab and long prefixes are quota-limited with preemption hint. Slab sizes are tuned by telemetry from the ledger.
5) Observability and alerts: emit per-GPU ledger metrics to Console with headroom trend, allocation rate, and eviction counts. Add an SLO alert when headroom falls below 1.2x median request footprint for >30s.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Conservative vs optimistic forecasting: conservative EWMA avoids OOMs but may reduce utilization. We will expose the smoothing factor as a knob per pool and provide recommended presets.
- Centralized accounting vs per-process ledgers: per-GPU ledgers avoid coordination latency but require robust consistency on process restart — we persist checkpoints to local disk every 10s.
- Eviction vs routing: aggressive eviction harms cache hit rates; prefer routing to lower-memory model variants when available and only evict cold KV entries as a last resort.

Acceptance criteria (quantitative):
- Ledger created and updated for every allocation in the runtime with <1% throughput overhead in microbenchmarks.
- In canary on staging with heavy KV workload: 30% reduction in p99 tail latency attributed to memory stalls vs baseline, and <1 OOM per 1M requests over 72h.
- Console shows per-GPU headroom dashboard and the alert fires during synthetic low-headroom tests.
- Router correctly routes to fallback variants under budget pressure in 95% of simulated overload cases.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (Week 1): proto ledger type and commit/rollback API; unit tests for counter invariants.
- M2 (Week 2): integrate ledger with allocator hooks (weights/resident pages, KV allocate/free, activation pool). Add local checkpointing.
- M3 (Week 3): request estimator in router + admission policy prototypes.
- M4 (Week 4): KV slab allocation and preemption hints.
- M5 (Week 5): Console metrics + alerts + canary in staging.

Risks & mitigation:
- Metric noise producing poor predictions — mitigate with configurable smoothing and heavy-weight canary telemetry.
- Race conditions on frees during preemption — add debug-only strict checking and fallback to conservative admission.
- User-visible rejects for P0 customers — default policy for high-tier customers is to route to dedicated capacity instead of reject.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Slate+Memory+Ledger+Design
- Proto PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- Perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/headroom-staging

Notes on rollout: start with a single GPU type pool in staging (A100-80GB equivalent). Observe ledger accuracy and adjust EWMA presets. After 1 week of stable canary, expand to other instance types with tuned knobs.

Operational playbook excerpt:
- If headroom alert triggers: check per-GPU ledger trends, recent deploys, and live allocation traces. Temporarily increase slab eviction aggressiveness or switch routing to lower-memory variant. If persistent, coordinate with Platform to spin up temporary Dedicated capacity.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: scoped and estimated. Decided to prototype ledger as in-process per-GPU data structure with checkpointing. Ava assigned as owner.
2026-03-03 - Design review: PMs recommended adding Console controls for emergency headroom. Design updated to include operator toggle and recommended presets. See design doc link.
2026-03-05 - Engineering update: M1 complete. Ledger type implemented and unit tests added (runtime/ledger). Observed <0.5% throughput overhead in synthetic alloc/free microbench.
2026-03-07 - Blocker noted: allocator free path needed small refactor to expose hooks. Working with allocator owners (ENG-14109 referenced) to merge change; temporary patch in PR #4521.
2026-03-08 - Performance note: initial EWMA smoothing factor (alpha=0.2) appears too conservative on bursty workloads. Will expose alpha as pool knob and test 0.5 in staging.
2026-03-09 - Integration: router estimator prototype added. Early canary sim shows correct re-routing to low-memory variant on 87% of cases; target 95% before rollout.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: finish KV slab allocator (M4) and wire metrics to Console (M5). Planning a staged canary the week of 2026-03-16.
